answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to return the jade of a valid state. A verifier challenges agents with random memory-access puzzles; failure to return data matching the echo of required sets triggers a penalty. Each instance must navigate the grove of unique bus access to prevent pooling. Honest agents pay 120 watts to maintain their status, while 1,000 fakes incur 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible.
